assumptions.summary: Individual time-trial starts are separated, so other riders do not affect the isolated rider.
Race energy is finite and no replenishment is modeled.
Air viscous resistance and ground rolling friction dominate; chain transmission loss is omitted.
The rider moves along a one-dimensional course coordinate and lateral width is ignored.
Weather enters through wind direction and speed; rain and snow are excluded.
Aerobic output is capped by FTP and the normalized aerobic pool is depleted through an exponential rate.
Anaerobic storage is finite and recovery is represented by a constant coefficient beta.
Sharp turns are speed checkpoints while soft turns are treated as straight course.

contributions.summary: Modify a three-Tank bioenergetic idea into explicit aerobic and anaerobic fatigue rates.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Male and female power-duration observations are fit by ordinary least squares; exact raw sample counts and residual diagnostics are not reported.
Olympics.com and Flanders2021 sources supply altitude and camber profiles for the named courses; the self-designed course is an experiment control.
Air density, effective area, drag coefficient, and rolling coefficient are assembled from cited aerodynamics and empirical constants.
Wind direction uses eight compass settings and wind speed uses 1, 2, and 3 m/s for a 24-case sensitivity grid.
NOAA Zeebrugge observation at 16:00 on 2021-09-19 supplies the guidance wind direction and 2 m/s speed.
The appendix displays women's track, power, speed, and energy panels but does not provide a complete executable implementation.

independent_extensions.summary: Fit a joint rider power-duration model with explicit energy states, unit checks, uncertainty, and held-out validation.

models.summary: Eq.1 maps aerobic output to an exponential fatigue rate under an FTP bound.
Eq.2 uses W_N/t for the anaerobic supplement.
Eq.4 defines a recovery speed using remaining aerobic capacity and beta.
Eq.5 takes the minimum inverse rate as the maintainable time.
Eq.6 uses a+W_N/t above FTP and -b ln(t)+c below FTP.
Eq.7 adds quadratic air drag and linear rolling friction.
Eqs.8-11 close air density, pressure-altitude, projected area, and drag coefficient.
Eq.12 balances motivation, resistance, gravity, and acceleration; Eq.13 marks corner positions.
The paper enumerates predecessor states and candidate powers, retaining the minimum feasible time at each discretized state.
Eq.14 passes wind angle and speed into the resistance term.
Eq.15 applies a position coefficient and Eq.16 marks draft events.

results_trace.summary: three-track comparison: Tokyo -> Belgium -> self-designed course -> male rider strategies. Boundary: Keep track geometry and rider type attached to every panel.
sprint-peak reading: sharp curve increase -> acceleration request -> sprint instruction. Boundary: A peak is interpreted through slope/turn context, not by shape alone.
recovery-dip reading: sharp curve drop -> reduced power -> anaerobic restoration. Boundary: Do not treat every dip as a compulsory recovery action without state evidence.
FTP-baseline reading: most positions -> near FTP -> stable aerobic power. Boundary: FTP is a reference level under the fitted rider model.
same-track shape invariance: rider types -> similar curve trends -> shared geometric response. Boundary: Similarity of trends does not imply equal power or finish time.
altitude-to-sprint interpretation: higher altitude -> variable gradients -> climb sprint/recovery cycles. Boundary: Separate reduced air resistance from increased gravity/gradient demand.
corner-power interpretation: corner checkpoint -> speed restriction -> power reduction. Boundary: The result inherits the binary corner model.
sprinter-versus-specialist contrast: first-half sprint peak -> later endurance decline -> type-specific strategy. Boundary: Keep the comparison conditional on selected parameter profiles.
corner-sensitivity contrast: dense Tokyo corners -> sprinter lower average power -> fewer cuts. Boundary: This interpretation needs the same checkpoint threshold and track geometry.
gender extension: male strategies -> female track cases -> appendix visual comparison. Boundary: Appendix figures extend the analysis without changing the core model.
weather-resistance result: wind direction -> adjusted air-relative speed -> completion time. Boundary: Wind results are scenario-grid outputs, not climatological risk estimates.
directional maximum: constant wind speed -> direction change -> 30-460 second change -> 16 percent. Boundary: Retain the baseline and direction increments behind the percentage.
speed-level effect: constant direction -> 1 m/s level change -> 20-330 second change -> under 10 percent. Boundary: Do not reconcile this result with a different table without checking baselines.
deviation construction: optimal curve -> random perturbation -> mean absolute deviation. Boundary: Random generation needs repetitions and a seed for reproducible inference.
deviation-table trend: deviation 0-0.2 -> finish time increase -> finite-energy failure. Boundary: Keep deviation units W/kg and distinguish delta seconds from percent.
near-optimal tolerance: small deviation -> less than 0.5 percent change -> practical tolerance. Boundary: A near-optimal band is a model output for the tested route and rider.
checkpoint guarantee: 11 route segments -> checkpoint time intervals -> no later than one minute. Boundary: List every checkpoint and ensure the guarantee matches the baseline finish time.
strength synthesis: fatigue model -> track factors -> team extension -> claimed generality. Boundary: Summarize mechanisms and scope together.
weakness synthesis: constant recovery -> simple turn model -> realism loss. Boundary: Keep the warning pass after positive evidence and name corrective tests.
draft/drop concept: six riders -> position coefficient -> draft rotation -> drop decision. Boundary: The extension is conceptual unless a full team solve is shown.

weaknesses.summary: Eq.1-Eq.6 do not fully specify energy normalization, rate-versus-state units, branch conditions, or recovery coupling.
The notation table labels P as a force unit while the equations use P for rider power, creating a symbol/unit conflict.
Eq.5 uses inverse rates for constant power but the recovery branch is not integrated into a variable-power state transition.
Eq.6 does not report fitted data, coefficient units, continuity derivation, or boundary behavior for a, b, and c.
The pressure-altitude and mass-based frontal-area/drag closures need dimensional and calibration checks.
R_T is used in both total-resistance and normal-force contexts in the force discussion, creating notation ambiguity.
Sharp turns are binary checkpoints and omit radius, braking distance, banking, and speed-transition dynamics.
Dynamic programming does not disclose state-grid resolution, transition step, convergence, runtime, or positivity safeguards.
Figure 13 wind-speed legend labels appear inconsistent with the text's 1, 2, and 3 m/s settings.
The deviation table and the prose statement about a 5% deviation causing a 10% time increase do not agree with the displayed values.
Table 5 says 11 segments but lists ten checkpoint distances, and the one-minute guarantee is not reconciled with the baseline.
The guidance contains '57h 19s' although the preceding baseline is 58m 19s, indicating a transcription error.
The self-designed course's start/end relationship is not numerically established as a closed route.
The team extension proposes draft/drop decisions but provides no solved schedule, calibration, or fourth-rider state transition.
